A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original automated evaluations on three datasets, human evaluations of generated images and dialogues, and a survey of 143 T2I users.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds a DesignBench experiment evaluating dialogue-based filtering of generated images.

M1.justification: V2 Appendix E.2 adds an auxiliary image-selection procedure: convert dialogue answers into binary VQA questions, score generated candidates, and select the highest-scoring image. The three main agents, their prompts, belief parsing, and transition procedures are retained; the expanded Algorithm 1 mainly restates existing operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same T2I tasks using COCO-Captions, ImageInWords, and the 30-scene DesignBench, alongside the retained human studies. The added filtering experiment uses existing DesignBench coverage. Newly documented participant eligibility does not establish a change in the recruited population.

E2.justification: V2 Section 6.3, footnote 2, newly reports qualitative comparisons against history-only prompting and minimal instructions such as 'ask a question,' finding them worse than principle-based prompting. The principal comparisons involving T2I, Ag1, Ag2, and Ag3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Appendix E.2 experiment generates ten candidates for each of 30 DesignBench ground-truth prompts, scores them using the first five Ag2 question-answer pairs, and compares average DINO similarity before and after selection. This adds a distinct evaluation procedure; the principal 15-turn evaluations, models, and automatic metrics are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted analysis of whether dialogue-derived VQA filtering mitigates the image generator's prompt-following errors. It also briefly reports the qualitative question-prompt ablation in Section 6.3. The existing agent comparisons, per-turn analyses, and illustrated dialogue cases remain.

E5.justification: V2 specifies ten different generation seeds for the new filtering experiment, without reporting uncertainty for its improvement. It also removes the explicit 'No Agreement' category and accompanying explanation from v1's human-ranking presentation. The existing Table 1 mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and three-rater counts are retained.

E6.justification: The automatic values in Table 1 are unchanged, but v2 adds dataset-specific human top-choice rates and reports DINO similarity of 0.7637 before versus 0.7838 after filtering under the new protocol. V1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 4 reverse Ag1 and Ag3's image-dialogue similarity distributions: their 'Very Close' rates change from approximately 64% and 52% to 52% and 64%. The earlier full content/style ranking distributions are no longer reported.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix C assumes that user intent remains fixed throughout interaction. V2 Appendix B instead assumes an intent identifiable in hindsight, corresponding to the image desired at the end. This revises a formal assumption while retaining the agent tuple, alignment objective, and heuristic scoring equation; no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: V2 drops the explicit first-of-its-kind contribution wording and dedicated novelty appendix, while retaining the central agent, belief-graph, evaluation-pipeline, and DesignBench contributions. Its introduction newly claims strong correlation between automatic and human evaluations. The principal performance and user-survey claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 narrows the belief graph's interpretation from a distribution over generated images to one over agent-generated image prompts. It explicitly acknowledges variation in users' importance judgments, explains Ag1 redundancy through belief-parsing errors, and discusses QA filtering as mitigation for the T2I model's fidelity bottleneck.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies ImageInWords starting-prompt summarization and image-conditioned caption creation for COCO and DesignBench. New Appendix H documents participant eligibility, desktop participation, consent, and stimulus screening. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that the retained studies changed; the detailed agent prompts and code/data access information remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Mehrabi et al. (2022) and distinguishes ambiguity resolution from underspecification, plus Basu and Bianchi references supporting cultural-bias motivation. It removes the dedicated multi-turn T2I discussion, including comparisons with Mini-DALLE3, AutoStudio, and Instruct-Imagen, and removes several references associated with the deleted novelty discussion. The broader research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around cultural context and a breakfast example. Belief graphs receive a separate section, agent descriptions move from the appendix into a dedicated main-text section, and transitions, experimental analysis, and appendices are reorganized. The novelty appendix is removed and an impact statement is added, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced, human-ranking charts give way to a new Table 1 column, and dialogue-result plots are redrawn with different orientation, grouping, legends, and axes. Algorithm 1 becomes full-width, and appendix interface figures are regrouped and resized. These substantially revise the visual presentation, although benchmark image grids and automatic evaluation curves are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves method exposition and documents data preparation and participant recruitment more clearly, while adding a focused filtering experiment. However, it removes detailed human-ranking and disagreement reporting and reverses Ag1/Ag3 attribution in the dialogue-similarity plot without explanation. The PDFs do not establish whether that reversal corrects or introduces an error. These benefits and unresolved effects on empirical reliability prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
